I've completed a thorough investigation of the current implementation. Before generating code I need to surface what already exists and lock down a few design decisions, because this feature touches the persistent `Chat`/`Message` models and the core agent loop.

# 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking

## Core Requirements
Introduce/reshape the **`agent`** chat mode so that:

1. The agent is driven by one or more **"knowledge" messages** that carry instructions: *what to do* and *definition of done*.
2. Task processing loops until one of three stoppers:
   - **Task solved** (agent signals done).
   - **Stopper condition** (user requests stop).
   - **`chat.estimation_cost` exceeded**.

## What already exists (important — avoids duplication)
The codebase already has most of the scaffolding. I traced each requirement:

| Requirement | Existing support | Gap |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `agent` chat mode | `CHAT_MODE_AGENT = "agent"`, `is_agent`, `_append_agent_message`, recursion loop in `_chat_with_project_inner` | No knowledge-driven instructions; loop only stops on `AGENT_DONE_WORD` or `max_iterations` |
| "Task solved" | `AGENT_DONE_WORD` sentinel (`globals.py`) checked in response content | — |
| "User stop" | `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY` + `CancellationToken` (`codx/junior/ai/cancellation.py`), `POST /api/chat/cancel`, `CancelledError` handled in `_chat_with_project_inner` | The recursive loop **does not check the token at iteration boundaries** — cancellation only surfaces while the AI is streaming |
| Cost tracking | `Analytics.record_token_usage(..., chat_id=...)`; `storage.read_events(chat_id=...)`; `get_chat_with_requests(chat_id)`; `TokenUsageEvent.total_cxjcoins` | No per-chat accumulated-cost helper exposed by `Analytics`; `get_total_usage()` does **not** accept `chat_id` |
| `estimation_cost` | ❌ Not present anywhere | Must be added to `Chat` (`db.py`) |

## Key findings that drive the design
- **`Chat` model** (`codx/junior/db.py`) has no cost/budget field. It uses `Optional[...] = Field(default=...)` patterns and `session_id`/`auto_initialize` as precedent → adding `estimation_cost` is low-risk and automatically flows through `POST /api/chats` (`Chat(**data)`).
- **`Message` model** has `role` (constants `ROLE_USER`/`ROLE_ASSISTANT`) and `task_item`. There is **no "knowledge" message type**, and `convert_message()` maps any non-`user` role to `AIMessage`, while `_build_message_history()` filters only `hide`/`improvement`. So a new `knowledge` role **will leak into the prompt history** unless explicitly handled.
- **The agent loop is recursive** (`_chat_with_project_inner` calls itself with `iteration+1`) and reuses the token registered at iteration 0. A cost/stop check must be added at the **top of each iteration**.
- **Cost is attributable per chat**: the engine already calls `ai.a_chat(..., chat_id=chat.id)`, and analytics records `chat_id`. Summing `total_cxjcoins` for `chat_id` gives the accrued chat cost.
- **`_resolve_profiles_and_model`** already forces `is_refine=True` when a profile declares it; `_resolve_chat_mode_flags` is the single place mode flags are derived.

## Strategic Approach (proposed)
1. **`db.py`** — add `Chat.estimation_cost: Optional[float]` (cxjcoins budget; `None` = unlimited) and a `ROLE_KNOWLEDGE = "knowledge"` constant (+ optional `Message` helper flag).
2. **`chat_engine.py`**
   - `_resolve_chat_mode_flags`: expose the resolved `estimation_cost` / a `cost_exceeded` helper.
   - New helper `_collect_agent_knowledge_messages(chat)` → concatenates `role == "knowledge"` messages (instructions + definition of done), in order.
   - `_append_agent_message`: inject the collected knowledge instructions + definition of done into the agent prompt.
   - `_build_message_history`: exclude `role == "knowledge"` messages from normal history (they are consumed separately as instructions).
   - New helper `_get_chat_accrued_cost(chat)` (sum `total_cxjcoins` for the chat via `Analytics`).
   - In `_chat_with_project_inner` loop: at the **top of each iteration**, evaluate the three stoppers — `cancellation_token.check()`, `cost_exceeded`, and `AGENT_DONE_WORD` — and stop cleanly with a closing assistant message + session-end analytics.
3. **`analytics.py` (optional)** — add a small `get_chat_cost(chat_id)` convenience (wraps `storage.read_events(chat_id=...)`).

## Dependencies & Risks
- **Message role leakage**: a `knowledge` role must be excluded from `_build_message_history`, `_build_clean_message_history_for_description`, and `_collect_files_from_visible_messages` (or handled deliberately).
- **Recursion + token reuse**: cost/stop checks must not double-register the token (registration is already guarded by `is_root_iteration`).
- **Cost timing**: `total_cxjcoins` is recorded *after* each AI call; the check is therefore evaluated between iterations (accurate at boundaries, not mid-stream).
- **Backward compatibility**: `estimation_cost=None` must preserve today's behavior exactly.
- **Two cancellation systems** exist (`ai.cancellation.CancelledError` vs `engine.agent_runtime.AgentCancelled`). The engine currently handles the former; the loop must reuse the registered `CancellationToken`.

## Target Files
| File | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| `codx/junior/db.py` | Modify — add `estimation_cost`, `ROLE_KNOWLEDGE` |
| `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py` | Modify — mode flags, knowledge injection, cost/cancel stoppers, loop control |
| `codx/junior/analytics/analytics.py` | Modify (optional) — `get_chat_cost(chat_id)` |

# 2. Minimum Changes Approach

I want your validation on the design below **before** generating full-file code, per the incremental workflow.

**A. `codx/junior/db.py`**
- Add `ROLE_KNOWLEDGE = "knowledge"` near `ROLE_USER`/`ROLE_ASSISTANT`.
- Add to `Chat`: `estimation_cost: Optional[float] = Field(default=None, description="Max cxjcoins allowed for agent processing; None = unlimited")`.
- *(Decision needed — see Q3)*: whether knowledge messages are identified by `role == "knowledge"` or by `task_item == "knowledge"`.

**B. `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py`**
- Extend `_resolve_chat_mode_flags` return dict with the resolved `estimation_cost`.
- Add `_collect_agent_knowledge_messages(chat)` → joins instructions + "definition of done".
- Update `_append_agent_message` to embed those instructions (alongside the existing `<task>`/`<parent_context>`/`<user_request>` and `AGENT_DONE_WORD`).
- Update `_build_message_history` and `_build_clean_message_history_for_description` to skip `knowledge` messages.
- Add `_get_chat_accrued_cost(chat)`.
- Update `_chat_with_project_inner` agent loop to stop on: `AGENT_DONE_WORD` **or** `cancellation_token.is_cancelled` **or** accrued cost ≥ `estimation_cost`, emitting a clear stop message and recording session end.

**C. `codx/junior/analytics/analytics.py`** *(optional)*
- Add `get_chat_cost(chat_id) -> float`.

# 3. Open Questions (missing information — please confirm)

To avoid inventing behavior, I need these decisions:

1. **`estimation_cost` unit & default** — is it **cxjcoins** (matching `TokenUsageEvent.total_cxjcoins`), and should `None` mean "unlimited" (preserve current behavior)? `[default: yes / unlimited]`
2. **Who sets `estimation_cost`** — the client via the existing `POST /api/chats` payload (no new endpoint needed), or should it be derived from the user's wallet/spending limit? `[default: client-set on Chat]`
3. **Knowledge messages representation** — new `Message.role = "knowledge"`, an existing `task_item` value, or a dedicated `Chat.agent_instructions` field? `[default: role="knowledge"]`
4. **Multiple knowledge messages** — ordered by insertion order and concatenated? Are they ever hidden/edited after creation? `[default: insertion order, concatenated]`
5. **Definition of done** — embedded as free text in the knowledge message, or a separate structured field? `[default: free text within knowledge message]`
6. **User stop mechanism** — reuse the existing `POST /api/chat/cancel` + `CancellationToken` (I'll add an explicit `check()` at each loop boundary), or a new sentinel word in an incoming message? `[default: reuse CancellationToken]`
7. **On stop, response behavior** — should the agent emit a final assistant message explaining the stop reason (cost/cancel) and persist it (crash-safe via `ChatEventBridge`), then end? `[default: yes]`
8. **Keep `max_iterations` cap?** — yes, as an additional safety net on top of the three stoppers. `[default: keep]`
9. **Cost aggregation source** — OK to sum `total_cxjcoins` via `Analytics.storage.read_events(chat_id=chat.id)`? `[default: yes]`

Once you confirm (or adjust) the defaults above, I'll generate the full updated contents of `db.py`, `chat_engine.py` (and the optional `analytics.py` helper) in the required code-block format with the per-file change summary tables.

"""
Unified logging, event emission and cancellation for agent runs.
Wraps openai_ai without modifying it: openai_ai's stream/tool callbacks
are adapted onto AgentRunContext.
"""
import json
import logging
import threading
import time
import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Iterator

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Errors
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class AgentCancelled(Exception):
    """Raised at checkpoints when the run has been cancelled."""


class InsufficientFundsError(Exception):
    """Raised by the wallet pre-flight check."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Cancellation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class CancellationToken:
    """Thread-safe cancellation token. cancel() may be called from any thread
    (e.g. a Socket.IO 'stop' handler) while the agent loop runs elsewhere."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._event = threading.Event()
        self.reason: str | None = None

    def cancel(self, reason: str = "user_requested"):
        self.reason = reason
        self._event.set()

    @property
    def cancelled(self) -> bool:
        return self._event.is_set()

    def raise_if_cancelled(self):
        if self._event.is_set():
            raise AgentCancelled(self.reason or "cancelled")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Events
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class AgentEventType(str, Enum):
    RUN_START = "run_start"
    RUN_END = "run_end"
    RUN_ERROR = "run_error"
    RUN_CANCELLED = "run_cancelled"
    LLM_REQUEST = "llm_request"
    LLM_CHUNK = "llm_chunk"
    LLM_USAGE = "llm_usage"
    TOOL_START = "tool_start"
    TOOL_END = "tool_end"
    TOOL_ERROR = "tool_error"
    TOOL_LOGS = "tool_logs"
    WALLET_CHECK = "wallet_check"


@dataclass
class AgentEvent:
    type: AgentEventType
    run_id: str
    project_id: str
    payload: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    ts: float = field(default_factory=time.time)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {"type": self.type.value, "run_id": self.run_id,
                "project_id": self.project_id, "ts": self.ts, **self.payload}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Analytics (tokens & tools) — fed automatically by emit()
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class RunAnalytics:
    prompt_tokens: int = 0
    completion_tokens: int = 0
    tool_calls: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # name -> {count, errors, total_ms}

    def on_event(self, event: AgentEvent):
        p = event.payload
        if event.type == AgentEventType.LLM_USAGE:
            self.prompt_tokens += p.get("prompt_tokens", 0)
            self.completion_tokens += p.get("completion_tokens", 0)
        elif event.type in (AgentEventType.TOOL_END, AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR):
            stats = self.tool_calls.setdefault(
                p.get("tool", "unknown"), {"count": 0, "errors": 0, "total_ms": 0.0})
            stats["count"] += 1
            stats["total_ms"] += p.get("duration_ms", 0.0)
            if event.type == AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR:
                stats["errors"] += 1

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        return {"prompt_tokens": self.prompt_tokens,
                "completion_tokens": self.completion_tokens,
                "total_tokens": self.prompt_tokens + self.completion_tokens,
                "tools": self.tool_calls}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Run context — the single object passed through the agent loop
# ------

"""
Chat + AI
This module is responsible for chat persistence and management.

Besides the classic full-chat ``save_chat``, this module now exposes granular,
merge-safe message operations (``add_message``, ``update_message``,
``remove_message``) used to persist chat changes *during* an AI turn (e.g.
tool-usage notification messages, streamed partial responses) without
overwriting concurrent updates.

It also provides full-text search capabilities via the ``search_chats`` method,
delegating to the ``ChatSearcher`` class for filtering by time frame, keyword
matching, and pagination.

Merge strategy (per message, keyed by ``doc_id``):

    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        A[Incoming chat messages] --> C{doc_id exists in stored chat?}
        B[Stored chat messages] --> C
        C -->|No| D[Keep message]
        C -->|Yes| E{parse incoming.updated_at >= parse stored.updated_at?}
        E -->|Yes| F[Keep incoming]
        E -->|No| G[Keep stored]
        D --> H[Merged message list]
        F --> H
        G --> H
    ```

CHANGED — timestamp normalisation:
    ``updated_at`` values historically exist in TWO formats:
    ``str(datetime.now())`` (space separator, Message default) and
    ``datetime.isoformat()`` (T separator, stamped by add/update_message).
    Comparing them as raw strings is WRONG ("...T..." always beats "... ..."
    lexicographically for the same day). :func:`_parse_timestamp` parses both
    formats so the last-writer-wins decision uses real datetimes.

CHANGED — persist hot-path:
    The granular operations are now called frequently mid-run (tool events,
    throttled stream persists). :meth:`ChatManager._load_stored_chat` reads
    the chat directly from ``chat.file_path`` when possible instead of
    scanning the whole tasks tree via ``find_by_id``.

NEW — chat search:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.search_chats` method provides full-text search
    across all chat data with optional time-frame filtering, user filtering,
    and pagination, delegating to :class:`codx.junior.chat_searcher.ChatSearcher`.

NEW — chat filtering:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.get_recent_chats` method now supports filtering by
    user_id, board, column, and chat_type (task or chat).

CHANGED — project_ids filtering:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.search_chats` method now supports filtering by
    project_ids list. When no query is provided, returns latest chats from
    accessible user projects.

CHANGED — chat ID validation:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.load_chat_from_path` method now ensures all loaded
    chats have a valid ID. Missing IDs are extracted from the filename or
    generated fresh, guaranteeing no chat is returned without an ID.

CHANGED — time-range filtering:
    :meth:`ChatManager.chat_paths` and :meth:`ChatManager.list_chats` now
    accept an optional **upper bound** (``before_update`` / ``to_date``) in
    addition to the existing lower bound (``last_update`` / ``from_date``),
    enabling an explicit ``[from_date, to_date]`` window. Both bounds are
    applied against the chat file ``mtime``. When a bound is ``None`` it is
    ignored, so existing callers are unaffected.
